name: Obsidian Cyan
reasoning: Near-black bases with steel borders read as engineered, not decorative. A single controlled cyan accent carries all interaction; everything else stays chromeless.
anti: Do not flood surfaces with the accent — cyan earns attention only on the primary action and active state.

name: Graphite Amber
reasoning: A warm graphite base feels crafted and expensive; amber gives it a human, editorial warmth without going soft.
anti: Avoid pure #000 — the warm base is the point; black kills the warmth.

name: Carbon Violet
reasoning: Violet-on-carbon is the default read for AI/ML surfaces; it supports subtle gradients without looking like a toy.
anti: Do not stack three neon gradients — one restrained violet glow beats a rave.

name: Slate Emerald
reasoning: Emerald signals growth and trust for money/health products while the slate base keeps it serious.
anti: Green must not double as both accent and success — pick distinct hues or users misread state.

name: Ink Crimson
reasoning: Cinematic crimson on ink is made for media and agency work where mood matters more than restraint.
anti: Crimson near danger-red confuses semantics — reserve a distinct danger tint.

name: Midnight Azure
reasoning: The safest enterprise dark theme: blue reads as trustworthy and secure without any risk-taking.
anti: This is the conservative pick — if the brief wants standout, choose a warmer or edgier palette.

name: Paper Noir
reasoning: Print-grade light theme where the type is the design; near-black text on warm paper, ink as its own accent.
anti: Do not add a colored accent — the restraint (ink-only) is the identity.

name: Arctic Indigo
reasoning: The reliable modern-SaaS light theme: cool neutrals, indigo action, generous air.
anti: Borders must stay subtle (#E2E8F0) — heavy borders make it feel like a form, not a product.

name: Sand Terracotta
reasoning: Warm organic neutrals for wellness/hospitality/boutique commerce — inviting, not corporate.
anti: Avoid pure white everywhere — the warm sand tint is what makes it feel boutique.

name: Cloud Rose
reasoning: Soft rose for consumer/creator products that want to feel welcoming and lightly playful.
anti: Keep the rose to accents/highlights — a fully pink UI reads juvenile.

name: Monochrome Steel
reasoning: Pure grayscale where white itself is the accent — maximum restraint, maximum craft signal.
anti: Introducing any hue breaks the concept; keep semantics (success/danger) muted and rare.

name: Deep Teal
reasoning: Cool teal on deep green-black is easy on the eyes for long dashboard sessions and reads as data-native.
anti: Teal and success-green sit close — separate them clearly in charts.
